descricao: The classic Brazilian carrot cake with chocolate frosting, made the way Tia Jô (Dani Noce's mother-in-law) makes it. Unlike American carrot cake, the carrots are blended into the batter, so the cake comes out bright orange, light and fluffy. The secret is weighing the peeled carrots: too much carrot makes the cake heavy and dense.

ingredientes.item: 9 1/2 oz carrots, peeled and washed (about 3 medium carrots)

ingredientes.nota: Any neutral oil, such as canola or vegetable oil, works too.
Tia Jô's original uses 2 cups. Dani cut it back a little for a less sweet cake.

ingredientes.item: 1 tablespoon light corn syrup or honey
ingredientes.nota: The original uses glucose syrup. Light corn syrup is the closest US equivalent.

modoDePreparo: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a cake pan.
Blend the carrots, oil, eggs and sugar in a blender for about 5 minutes, until completely smooth.
Pour into a bowl, sift in the flour and baking powder, and stir until combined.
Bake for about 50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.
Bring the butter and corn syrup (or honey) to a boil.
Pour it over the chopped chocolate and let it sit for 3 minutes.
Stir or blend until smooth and glossy.
Pour the ganache over the cake.
dicas: Fewer dishes: once the first mixture is blended, add the flour and baking powder straight to the blender and pulse just until combined. Dani has made it this way with great results.
Cut the carrots into chunks before blending so the blender can handle them easily.
The total time includes about 30 minutes for the cake to cool before frosting.
The cake keeps for up to 3 days.

credito.observacao: Translated from Portuguese and converted to US measurements.
